text:
Sara: Heads up — noticed a regression on staging where KV cache memory climbs steadily on long-context traces when continuous-batching is enabled. repro starts at ~30m.
Michael: hmm, when you say climbs do you mean total RSS or resident pages pinned by KV cache?
Sara: resident pages. RSS follows. Looks like certain pages never get released after merges/splits in the batch path.
Jin: do you have a flamegraph or pprof? can we see where the refcounts are held?
Sara: yes, I ran pprof on the worker. here's the gist: `go tool pprof -png /tmp/prof.cpu /app/bin/runtime` -> uploaded to buildkite. ops-bot linked it: https://artifacts.internal/pprof/2136000000/kv-longctx-merge.png
ops-bot: Uploaded pprof: kv-longctx-merge.png (sha256:fa3b...)
Priya: quick glance — there's a hot path in batch.merge_batches -> kvcache::retain_page -> slot_ref::pin
Carlos: that pin graph looks like it's coming from merge_map handling. we recently changed merge_map to keep page refs until post-commit to avoid races. could be over-retaining.
Michael: I remember that change — it deferred release to avoid double-free during split. but on long contexts continuous-batching produces many merge/split cycles, so the deferred-release pileup could blow memory.
Jin: we should confirm whether the pileup is from merges only or from repeated split+merge oscillation (i.e., livelock holding head-of-line). can someone run a simple repro with logging for merge_map size and pin count?
Sara: running now on a staging worker with verbose KV debug. also added a metric: kvcache.merge_map.len and kvcache.pinned_pages.count
Sara: logs so far: at t=00:18:32 merge_map.len=172, pinned_pages.count=380, kv_total_pages=4096
Priya: that's very high. does pinned_pages.count decrease after merges finish? or it stays constant?
Sara: stays high — even during idle periods. we see merge_map entries with state=WAITING_FOR_SPLIT and state=MERGED_HOLD
Carlos: that suggests the state machine isn't transitioning to RELEASE on some code paths — maybe an early return on error.
Michael: can you grep for places where merged entries early-return before release? maybe on timeout/fallback paths.
Jin: also check continuous-batch heuristics — we have a path that coalesces small batches into a “head batch” while other requests spin waiting. head-of-line blocking could keep the head batch alive and its KV refs pinned until it finally drains.
Priya: I can reproduce an artificial sequence: spawn many small requests with long prefix so KV pages get loaded, then have continuous-batcher merge them. results: merge_map grows, pinned_pages climbs, and tail requests get starved.
Sara: attaching small repro script snippet:
```
# stress.sh
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"'"$(printf 'A%.0s' {1..500})"'","max_tokens":1}' &
done
wait
```
Carlos: thanks. i ran that under profiler and got repeated stack traces stuck in kv_page_pin -> batch.wait_for_head -> merge_batches
Michael: hypothesis: merge_batches keeps a strong ref for the head group's KV pages until every merged sub-batch is processed; if a sub-batch is stalled (network/IO), head stays alive -> hol livelock.
Jin: two mitigation ideas:
- (A) make merge_map hold weak refs and bump to strong only when actually needed for execution (defer pinning)
- (B) add a GC pass that times out stale merge_map entries and force-release pins if they've been WAITING > X ms
Priya: (B) sounds safer short-term. (A) requires careful concurrency to avoid race conditions.
Michael: agree. also consider changing batching heuristic: cap merge depth or prefer splitting large head batches when they exceed memory pressure threshold.
Sara: i instrumented memory-pressure signals: when mem_pressure>0.7 we still merge by default. we could add config: continuous_batch.max_merge_pages and fallback_strategy=split_on_pressure
Carlos: I pushed a quick prototype implementing (B): timeout-based release (default 250ms). ran it on staging, pinned_pages peaked lower and then reclaimed; long-run looks better — still verifying throughput impact.
ops-bot: Deploy started: kvcache-reclaim-timeout-proto -> staging (build 2136000012)
Jin: nice. can you share before/after pprof traces? also capture alloc_objects for KV pages.
Sara: before: pinned_pages steady 420. after prototype: steady ~80 and merge_map.len rarely >20. pprof shows much less time in retain_page.
Priya: any regressions in latency tail? timeout could release pages prematurely and cause page misses.
Carlos: i ran synthetic workload; 95th latency increased 10% for tiny prompts but median unchanged. need to test with real long-context traces.
Michael: if we go with (B) for now, add a feature flag and metric for forced_releases so we can monitor.
Jin: longer term (A) + smarter batching: treat KV page weight as part of batching heuristic so merges that would pin >N pages are disallowed.
Sara: created a ticket: RT-9843 with notes + repro + staging job links. will iterate.
Priya: i'll help with the A design, specifically weak_ref -> on-demand promote pattern. careful with ABA on refcounts.
Michael: great. next steps: (1) keep prototype reclaim-timeout behind flag, (2) run 24h long-context soak, (3) design batching heuristic with page-weight cost model, (4) consider kernel selection knobs to avoid heavy slow-paths during these merges.
Sara: thanks all. added follow-up meeting Thurs 11am to review soak results. :white_check_mark:
